label: To Be Or Not to Be

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Another job well done.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: All traces of the D-Wave have completely disappeared.
... I see.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: We were able to probe the memories of the mass-produced Nikke you were with.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I believe the sobriquet you all gave her was 6000-D.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: In doing that,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: we learned the reason behind the sudden reappearance of the D-Wave.
Does it also explain why the factory materialized out of nowhere?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: A few months ago...
We sent a Nikke squad out to the factory up on the surface.
Their mission was to retrieve any and all viable resources that could be used for the war effort.
Included in the ranks of this squad was a mass-produced Nikke that you all now know as 6000-D.
Due to the fact we had not detected any Rapture presence in the area,
the squad deployed was assembled entirely of mass-produced Nikkes.
However, once they breached the factory, they walked straight into a Rapture ambush.
They fought hard,
and succeeded in defeating all but one of the Raptures.
6000-D was the lone survivor. The rest of her squadmates were wiped out.

lines.speaker: 6000d_02
lines.text: *Huff huff*
The sole remaining Rapture and 6000-D were locked in their final battle.
Determined to survive, she fought with everything she had.
She used her last bullet to destroy the Rapture's core,
and as soon as the core was destroyed...
*Kreeeeeee*
The D-Wave emitted by the Gatekeeper surged forth towards 6000-D and the fallen Rapture.

lines.speaker: 6000d_02
lines.text: What was that?
She looked all around her, but couldn't detect anything unusual in her surroundings.
She set aside her feelings of anxiety and pulled her broken and battered body up off the ground.
Just as she intended to return to the Ark...
*Thud*
Two transporters came down.

lines.speaker: 6000d_02
lines.text: What the... What is this?
*Thud*
A burst of light enveloped the two transporters, and two individuals came flying out as they tumbled to the ground.

lines.speaker: 6000d_02
lines.text: Are they humans? Or Nikkes?
Her memories of this particular moment were damaged, so it remains somewhat unclear,
but we are fairly certain these two, one female and one male, are the androids you met: 2B and 9S.
*Shaaaaa*
The previously blinding light emanating from the transporters subsided.
But then nothing happened.
6000-D looked around with no small amount of apprehension.
*Kaboom*
From far off, there was the sound of something falling.
But nothing further happened.
Scared out of her mind, 6000-D attempted to get out of the factory.
At that moment,
numerous mysterious doors appeared before her, all of them enveloped in light.
The doors on the right started shining and Raptures began spilling out of them.
*Thud thud thud thud*

lines.speaker: 6000d_02
lines.text: Th-this can't be!

lines.speaker: 6000d_02
lines.text: How can there be so many?!
6000-D thought that she was done for.
That was, however, until the doors on the left started to shine as well,
and a barrage of Product 12 model mass-produced Nikkes spilled out.

lines.speaker: 6000d_02
lines.text: Nikkes...?
The Raptures and the mass-produced Nikkes that emerged from the doors started shooting at each other, with no one paying her any heed.
As the two sides filled the factory,
they kept repeating the same internecine cycle again and again: generate from the doors, fight, and die.
Rinse and repeat.
Before B-6000's eyes,
all she saw was an endless cycle of death and destruction.
Raptures born to kill Nikkes,
and mass-produced Nikkes, who looked exactly like her,
born to kill Raptures.
This macabre display went on for a week.

lines.speaker: 6000d_02
lines.text: Ah!

lines.speaker: 6000d_02
lines.text: I can't take it anymore.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Our speculation is that at that moment, she experienced a Mind Switch.
... I see.
So by the time we met her, the Mind Switch had already taken place.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Most likely, yes.
Why do you think the Gatekeeper replicated 6000-D and the Rapture?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: We don't have any access to the Gatekeeper's memory.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: This is pure speculation,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: but I believe it may have purely been because it was intrigued.
Intrigued?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Intrigued by the sight of 6000-D desperately fighting the Rapture.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Perhaps the Gatekeeper manufactured the Raptures and the mass-produced Nikkes in order to recreate that scene.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: And in order to help make that happen, it attempted to copy the technology harnessed by those Androids from another world.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: It called upon them using their own transporters,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: thereby bringing 2B and 9S to our world.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: It then proceeded to use that transporter to create

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: the mysterious doors that we saw producing both the Raptures and the Nikkes.
I see.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: That's all.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Do you have any questions?
Upon being asked if I have any questions,
I think back on the recent events at the factory.
After the death of 6000-D, C-1002 was inconsolable.
She sat in front of 6000-D's lifeless body and stared up into the air.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: What am I going to do now?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: B-0006... 6000-D... they're all dead.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Do I even deserve to be alive?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: I either want a memory wipe,

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: or I want to die.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: {AccountData.NickName}.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: What should I do?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: You're a human, the only one amongst us here.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Since humans are the ones who made Nikkes, I'm asking you...

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: please decide what I should do with my life.

lines.speaker: rapi
lines.text: You...!

lines.speaker: neon
lines.text: What?!

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: What are you saying?!

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: How could you ask the Commander such a thing?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Please.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: I'm begging you.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Help me.
Death is not the answer. You'll be able to overcome it while you're still alive.
If these are memories that you cannot bear, then erasing them might be the best answer.
Don't say anything.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: While I'm still alive...?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Heh... hehe...

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Hahaha!

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: So you want me to live the rest of my life in misery, is that it?

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: How can you say that?!
It's okay, Anis.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: The hell it is!

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: One day...

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Yes,

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: everything might get better.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: One day...

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: *Sob*

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: *Sob*

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: All right. I will try.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: I'll try to go on.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Maybe I will get better one day.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Thank you for listening... and thank you for helping me come to a decision.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Are you okay?
... What happened to C-1002?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Oh, her?
Well?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: She... was disposed of.
No...

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: After coming back from her mission,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: not only did she insist on others referring to her as C-1002,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: she also filed numerous requests to verify if she had a human brain.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: She was showing the initial warning signs of becoming an Irregular.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Given 6000-D's diagnosis of having undergone a Mind Switch,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: it didn't take much of a leap for the Central Government to decide that C-1002 was experiencing the same malfunction.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: They therefore decided to dispose of her, or so I heard.
... Understood.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Yes... that has to be the best option.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: To live holding onto such traumatic memories...

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: I couldn't bear it.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Thank you for listening... and thank you for helping me come to a decision.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: With a memory wipe,

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: I'll be able to forget everything.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: All of what happened here...

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: I was so happy to get my own name.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: So happy to have friends who were the same model as me...

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Why... why did things have to end like this?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Why?!

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: *Sob*

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: *Sob*

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: *Sob*

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Are you okay?
... What happened to C-1002?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Oh, her?
Well?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Upon her request, she was granted a memory wipe.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Afterwards, I believe she went back up to the surface.
For another mission?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Yes, to retrieve any and all viable resources that could be used for the war effort.
What?!
After all she went through, they're assigning her a mission similar to 6000-D's?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I don't know if this was the intention of the superiors,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: but she indeed was assigned to a remarkably similar mission.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: All we can do is hope that she returns safe and unharmed.
... Yes.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Why aren't you saying anything?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Sa-say something.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Please, anything.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Please just say something!

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: C-1002, what is all of this about?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: You're a human.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: You have no idea of the misery we're subjected to.

lines.speaker: rapi
lines.text: C-1002, stop!

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Why can't you just say something?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Think of me as any other mass-produced Nikke passing by during a routine mission.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Or as one of those Nikkes who died inside the factory.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Just as long as you say something,

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: you can give me the smallest shred of guidance.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: That-That's all I ask.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Surely you can do that much?

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: *Sob*

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Don't leave me alone with my misery.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: Or I'll despise you for as long as I live.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: I'm not going back.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: I'm abandoning my mission. Kill me if you have to. I understand.

lines.speaker: c1002_02
lines.text: I'm sick and tired of this endlessly repeating cycle that is my life.
C-1002 walks out of the factory.
She's clearly given everything up. None of us move to stop her.
All we can do is watch her leave.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Are you okay?
... Is there still no news about C-1002?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Nothing. We haven't been able to find her.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: There haven't been any reports of her returning to the Ark,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: nor any sightings of her up on the surface.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: However...
What is it?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Near the factory, it appears there were

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: the remains of a Product 12 model that was beset upon by Raptures.
Don't tell me...

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: We haven't confirmed that it's C-1002.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: The head was completely destroyed, which made it impossible to search its memory.
Damn...

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: All we can do is hope that it wasn't her.
... Yes.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I keep feeling like I'm the bearer of bad news,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: but is there anything else that you want to ask?
... No, there isn't anything else.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Very well. Then that is all.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Congratulations on another job well done.
The truth hurts, and I've had my fill of it today.
Forcing my aching limbs to lurch me forward, I head towards the Outpost.
*Sigh*
Rubbing my tired eyes, I'm about to enter the Commander's Room...

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: ... Rapi.
When I hear voices from inside.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: When I saw that

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: hollowed out head in the factory,

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: I started wondering if there really was a brain in my head.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: I wanted to get a brain scan.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: To make sure I still have the same brain from when I was a human.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: To make sure that...

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: that I'm really Anis.

lines.speaker: rapi
lines.text: ... Anis.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: I know, I know. I'm still me.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: I love soda.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: I'm a lazybones.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: Even if the brain I have now isn't the same as I was when I was human,

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: I'm still me. I'm Anis.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: It's as simple as that.

lines.speaker: anis
lines.text: ... Right?
*Plop*
Realizing now isn't a good time to enter the Commander's Room, I sit on the floor.
What truly defines me as myself?
What makes me "me"?
My brain?
My body?
The finite nature of my existence?

lines.speaker: b0006_02
lines.text: Then do you have

lines.speaker: b0006_02
lines.text: a human brain like we do?

lines.speaker: ce_02_npc_01
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: ce_02_npc_01
lines.text: We don't have that.

lines.speaker: ce_02_npc_01
lines.text: We don't have human brains. We have consciousness data instead.

lines.speaker: b0006_02
lines.text: Don't have human brains...

lines.speaker: b0006_02
lines.text: but you seem so...

lines.speaker: b0006_02
lines.text: human.
Even without a human brain...

lines.speaker: ce_02_01
lines.text: I don't want anyone else to influence my thought process

lines.speaker: ce_02_01
lines.text: which might result in me making a hasty decision.
we all need to determine the path to our own life.

lines.speaker: ce_02_npc_01
lines.text: You've been fighting non-stop. Aren't you tired?

lines.speaker: ce_02_01
lines.text: So far so good.

lines.speaker: ce_02_npc_01
lines.text: Well, don't push yourself too hard.

lines.speaker: ce_02_01
lines.text: You too.
We must care for one another.

lines.speaker: ce_02_npc_01
lines.text: Farewell, everyone.

lines.speaker: ce_02_01
lines.text: I hope you all achieve what you're after.
We are beings who share our feelings with strangers from other worlds.

lines.speaker: ce_02_01
lines.text: Even if everything is predetermined,

lines.speaker: ce_02_01
lines.text: that to me doesn't negate the value of your individual feelings. Your sadness belongs to you, and you alone.
It's as she said.
Leading an existence in which you are true to yourself is what's most important.
Whether or not you have a human brain,
or what your body is made of.
Whether your life will come to a natural end.
Whether you have the capacity for rational thought or to feel emotions.
The answers to all these questions may well lie
with those two Androids who were part of our mission.
As I sit down in the empty hallway,
I think about those who have left us.
